## Google Business Profile Verification Documents in India 2026

The Google Business Profile verification documents India businesses need depend on the verification method Google offers and the type of business being verified. Common supporting evidence includes a GST certificate, Shop and Establishment registration, Udyam registration, trade licence, utility bill, permanent signage, branded equipment, and a live video showing the business operates at the stated location.

Verification is not simply a document-upload exercise. Google is checking whether a real business exists, whether it is eligible for a profile, and whether the business information shown on Google Maps can be connected to that business. The exact options and evidence requested can differ between a shop, office, clinic, school, NGO, home-service business, and service-area business.

## What Google Business Profile Verification Means

Google Business Profile, often called GBP, is the business listing that can appear in Google Search and Google Maps. It may show the business name, category, address or service area, phone number, website, hours, photos, reviews, and other details.

Verification gives the business owner control over the profile and helps Google reduce fake, duplicate, misleading, or automatically generated listings. It does not guarantee a particular ranking in local search. It also does not replace compliance with local registrations, tax requirements, professional licensing, or sector-specific rules.

Google decides which verification methods are available for a profile. These methods can include:

- Video recording submitted through the GBP dashboard
- Live video call with a Google representative
- Phone call or SMS
- Email
- Postcard by mail
- Additional document or business information requests

Not every business will see every method. The options may change after edits to the profile, failed attempts, changes in ownership, or a request for additional verification.

### Why verification can be difficult in India

Indian businesses operate through many different structures. A business may be registered as:

- A sole proprietorship
- A partnership firm
- A limited liability partnership
- A private limited company
- A trust or society
- A Section 8 company
- An unregistered small business operating under the owner’s name
- A home-based or mobile service
- A franchise or branch of a larger organisation

The legal name on a document may not match the public-facing brand name. For example, a bakery may operate under a brand name while its GST registration is in the proprietor’s name. A clinic may use a doctor’s name in one registration and a clinic name on its signboard. This does not automatically make the business ineligible, but the evidence should clearly connect the legal entity, brand, location, and services.

## Google Business Profile Verification Documents in India

There is no single universal document list that applies to every Indian business. Google normally tells you what evidence is required during the verification flow. Submit the requested evidence first, rather than uploading a random collection of documents.

The following documents can be useful depending on the business and the verification request.

### GST registration certificate

A GST registration certificate can help establish the registered business name, trade name, address, and GSTIN. It is often useful for shops, manufacturers, agencies, distributors, D2C businesses, clinics with applicable registrations, and other formal enterprises.

Check that:

- The address is current
- The legal name or trade name is understandable in relation to the profile name
- The document is complete and readable
- The business category and location are not inconsistent with the profile
- Sensitive information is not unnecessarily exposed when the upload does not require it

A GST certificate alone may not prove that a customer-facing location currently operates there. Google may still request signage, a live video, or other evidence.

### Shop and Establishment registration

In Maharashtra, businesses commonly refer to Shop and Establishment registration or the relevant labour and establishment registration process as “Shop Act” or “Gumasta” registration. Similar registrations exist under different names in other states.

This document may help establish that a business operates from a particular address. It is particularly relevant for retail shops, offices, salons, small agencies, restaurants, and local service businesses.

The document should be current where validity or renewal applies. If the business has moved, the address on the registration should not be relied on without updating it.

### Udyam Registration Certificate

Udyam Registration can support the identity of a micro, small, or medium enterprise. It may show the enterprise name, organisation type, and registered address.

It is useful supporting evidence, but it should not be treated as automatic proof that Google must approve a particular listing. A home-based enterprise, online business, or service provider may still need to show that it has a legitimate customer-facing operation or serves customers at their locations.

### Trade licence and municipal documents

A municipal trade licence, local business licence, establishment permission, or other authority-issued document may be relevant for:

- Restaurants and food businesses
- Retail shops
- Salons and wellness centres
- Workshops
- Clinics and diagnostic centres
- Schools, coaching centres, and activity centres
- Businesses that require local permission to operate

The document should relate to the business being listed and, where possible, show the same address or a clearly connected address.

### FSSAI registration or licence

Food businesses in India may have an FSSAI registration or licence. This can support the identity and operation of a restaurant, cloud kitchen, bakery, caterer, food manufacturer, or packaged-food business.

However, FSSAI evidence does not by itself establish whether the profile should display a storefront address. A cloud kitchen or delivery-only food operation may need to follow different GBP eligibility and address-display rules from a restaurant that receives customers at its premises.

### MCA and incorporation documents

Companies and LLPs may use documents such as:

- Certificate of Incorporation
- LLP incorporation certificate
- Company master data
- Registered office records
- Partnership deed, where relevant
- Business PAN or other official tax records

These documents can connect a legal entity with its name and registered address. They may not prove that the location is open to customers or that a particular brand operates there. If the profile uses a brand name that differs from the incorporation name, provide additional evidence that links the brand to the entity.

### Utility bills and address evidence

Recent electricity, internet, water, landline, or other business utility bills may be requested as address evidence. The bill should generally show:

- The business or responsible person’s name
- The address
- The issuing provider
- A recent date
- Clear, unedited information

An owner’s name on a utility bill may be acceptable as supporting evidence for a sole proprietorship or home-based business, but the relationship between the person and the business should be clear. A utility bill alone does not prove that customers can visit the location.

### Lease, rent, or ownership documents

A registered lease, rent agreement, property tax document, or ownership record can help explain why the business is operating at an address. These documents are more useful when combined with visible branding, business equipment, and a clear video of the premises.

Do not submit private property documents unless they are necessary for the verification request. Where possible, share only the relevant pages and protect sensitive personal or financial information, provided that doing so does not make the document unusable.

## Which Documents Are Best for Different Indian Businesses?

The strongest evidence is usually a combination of official business identity and physical or operational evidence. The right combination depends on whether customers visit the location, whether staff work there, and whether the business travels to customers.

| Business type | Useful official evidence | Useful operational evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Retail shop | GST, Shop and Establishment registration, trade licence | Exterior signboard, entrance, shelves, billing counter, products |
| Restaurant or bakery | FSSAI, GST, municipal licence | Signage, kitchen, dining area, menu, equipment |
| Clinic or diagnostic centre | Applicable professional or local registration, GST where relevant | Signboard, reception, consultation rooms, equipment |
| School or coaching centre | Registration or education-related permissions where applicable | Building signage, classrooms, reception, staff access |
| NGO or charitable organisation | Trust deed, society registration, Section 8 documents, tax records | Office sign, name board, work materials, staff area |
| Agency or consultancy | GST, Udyam, incorporation or establishment records | Office sign, workstation, branded materials, client-facing entrance |
| D2C or home-based brand | GST, Udyam, business registration | Packaging, inventory, branded labels, workspace, dispatch process |
| Service-area business | Business registration or tax document | Vehicle branding, tools, uniforms, storage, service operations |
| Franchise or branch | Brand authorisation, local registration, GST or lease evidence | Branch signboard, interior, staff, branded premises |

This table is a planning guide, not a guaranteed acceptance list. Google’s verification screen and policies take priority.

## Verification Methods and What to Show

### Video verification

Video verification is common when Google wants visual proof that the business exists. The recording is normally submitted from the GBP interface, and the instructions shown there should be followed exactly.

A useful video may need to establish three things:

1. The location or area is real and identifiable.
2. The business has access to that location or operates from it.
3. The business provides the services or sells the products described on the profile.

Depending on the business, the recording may show:

- Street signs, nearby landmarks, or building numbers
- The exterior of the premises
- Permanent business signage
- The entrance and interior
- Staff-only or operational areas
- Business equipment and inventory
- A billing system or appointment system
- Branded packaging and dispatch materials
- A vehicle, tools, or uniforms for a mobile business

Do not create a staged video that hides the real nature of the business. Do not show confidential customer records, payment details, medical information, passwords, or private documents that are not needed.

### Live video call

A live video call may involve showing the premises and business operations in real time. The person conducting the call should be authorised to represent the business and should be able to explain the relationship between the public brand name and the legal documents.

Keep the relevant documents available, but do not assume that displaying every document will resolve a mismatch. The address, signage, category, and actual operation should be consistent.

### Phone or SMS verification

If phone or SMS verification is offered, the number should be controlled by the business and able to receive the verification code. A shared call centre number, an inactive landline, or a number that cannot receive the code can create delays.

For multi-location businesses, each location should have accurate contact information. Do not create multiple profiles merely to use different phone numbers if the locations are not genuinely separate and eligible.

### Email verification

Email verification may be available for some businesses. Use an email address that is connected to the business domain or otherwise clearly controlled by the organisation when possible. A free email address does not automatically make a profile invalid, but a business-domain address may make ownership easier to explain.

### Postcard verification

Postcard verification, where available, sends a code to the listed address. The business must be able to receive mail at that location. Do not edit the address while waiting unless the dashboard or Google support instructs you to do so, because changes can interrupt the process.

Postcard verification confirms access to the address. It does not by itself settle every eligibility question, such as whether the business is allowed to show a storefront address or whether the profile is a duplicate.

## How to Prepare Before Starting GBP Verification

Preparation reduces avoidable problems.

### Confirm eligibility

A business generally needs meaningful in-person contact with customers during its stated operating hours. Businesses that exist only online may not qualify for a Business Profile in the same way as a local business with customer contact.

A service-area business can often serve customers at their locations without displaying a public address. A virtual office, mailbox, rented meeting room used occasionally, or co-working address with no genuine business presence can create problems. Do not list an address simply because it is in a desirable commercial area.

### Use the real-world business name

The profile name should normally reflect how the business is known in the real world. Adding keywords, neighbourhood names, phone numbers, slogans, or services to the name can violate Google’s guidelines.

For example, a business should not add phrases such as “Best Digital Marketing Agency in Pune” to its actual name unless that wording is genuinely used as the business name on its signage and business materials.

### Select an accurate primary category

The primary category should describe the main business activity. Additional categories can describe meaningful secondary services, but they should not be used to target every related search.

A clinic, school, NGO, restaurant, and marketing agency each have different evidence patterns. An inaccurate category can make the documents and video appear inconsistent.

### Check address consistency

Compare the address across:

- GBP
- GST or business registration
- Website
- Signboard
- Invoices
- Social profiles
- Local directories
- Lease or utility documents

Indian addresses may use different formats, abbreviations, nearby landmarks, PIN codes, or building descriptions. Minor formatting differences are not always a problem, but major differences should be explained or corrected.

### Prepare permanent signage

For a storefront profile, the business name should be visibly displayed at the entrance or premises. Temporary paper signs, loose banners, or a sign that does not match the profile name may be weak evidence.

The signboard should not falsely suggest that a business occupies a space it does not use. In a shared building, identify the correct floor, office, unit, or reception area where appropriate.

## Common Reasons for Verification Failure

### Brand and legal name do not connect

A brand name on Google and a proprietor or company name on the GST certificate can be different. The issue is not necessarily the difference itself; it is the lack of evidence connecting them.

Use supporting materials such as branded invoices, website ownership, packaging, signage, authorisation letters, or registration records where relevant. Keep the explanation factual and concise.

### The address is a virtual office or mailbox

A virtual address may receive mail but lack staff, equipment, signage, or customer operations. This can be unsuitable for a storefront profile. If the business travels to customers, consider whether a service-area profile better reflects the operation.

### There is no visible business identity

A home-based business can be legitimate, but a video showing only a residential door may not establish the business. Show appropriate business operations without exposing private household areas. Branded packaging, inventory, equipment, a work area, and dispatch activity may help where relevant.

### The business category does not match the evidence

A profile listed as a restaurant but showing only packaged-product storage, or a clinic profile with no visible clinical operation, can raise questions. Choose the category that accurately reflects what customers can experience.

### Duplicate profiles exist

Creating several profiles for one location, one business, or slightly different versions of the name can make verification more difficult. Search Google Maps before creating a new profile. If a listing already exists, claim or request access to it instead of starting another one.

### Documents are unclear or outdated

Blurry scans, cropped pages, expired registrations, old addresses, and screenshots without context are weak evidence. Use readable files and current information. Avoid editing documents beyond reasonable redaction of sensitive data.

### Repeated verification attempts are made without fixing the issue

Submitting the same incomplete evidence multiple times may not help. First identify whether the problem is the address, business name, category, eligibility, duplicate status, or ownership. Then correct the underlying information before trying again.

## What to Do After a Failed Verification

Read the exact message in the GBP dashboard. It may indicate a problem with the address, ownership, eligibility, or the verification method.

Review the profile against Google’s Business Profile guidelines and the business’s actual operation. Do not change the business name, address, and category repeatedly just to trigger another method. Unnecessary edits can make the profile harder to assess.

Prepare a short explanation covering:

- The legal or trading name of the business
- The actual operating address or service area
- The relationship between the brand and legal entity
- Whether customers visit the location
- The documents and video evidence being supplied
- Any reason for an address or name difference

If an appeal or additional review option is available in the dashboard, use that process. Keep records of the profile URL, registration documents, previous messages, and dates of submissions. Only an authorised owner or representative should communicate with Google about the listing.

## Protecting Business and Customer Information

Verification evidence can contain sensitive information. This is especially important for clinics, schools, NGOs, and businesses handling customer data.

Before submitting:

- Remove unrelated personal information where acceptable
- Do not display Aadhaar numbers, bank details, passwords, or payment credentials
- Avoid showing patient files, student records, donor information, or customer addresses
- Do not include confidential contracts unless requested
- Use official upload channels rather than sending documents to unknown agents
- Restrict access to the Google account and enable strong account security

A marketing agency helping with GBP should use proper access permissions rather than asking for a client’s personal Google password. The business owner should retain ownership of the profile and recovery details.

## GBP Verification and Local SEO in India

Verification is only the foundation of local SEO. A verified listing can still perform poorly if the information is incomplete, inaccurate, or inconsistent.

After verification, review:

- Business name, address, phone number, and website
- Primary and secondary categories
- Hours, holiday hours, and appointment links
- Services and products
- Photos of the actual premises or work
- Service areas, where applicable
- Review responses
- Duplicate or outdated listings
- Website contact and location information

For Indian businesses, also check practical details customers use before visiting. These may include landmark information, parking instructions, language options, WhatsApp contact, appointment requirements, delivery coverage, and whether the location is open to walk-ins.

Do not add false locations or use rented addresses only to appear in another locality. Local SEO works best when the profile reflects the way the business genuinely serves customers.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What documents are accepted for Google Business Profile verification in India?

There is no universal document list for every profile. Google may request a GST certificate, Shop and Establishment registration, Udyam certificate, trade licence, FSSAI licence, utility bill, lease evidence, or other proof, along with visual evidence of the business. The verification screen and Google’s instructions for that profile should be treated as the final requirement.

### Is a GST certificate mandatory for GBP verification?

No, a GST certificate is not automatically mandatory for every business. Some small businesses may not be GST-registered or may be operating under a structure where other evidence is more relevant. Google can still ask for proof of business identity, location, access, or operations through another document or verification method.

### Can I verify a home-based business in India?

A home-based business may be eligible if it has genuine customer contact and follows Google’s rules. If customers do not visit the home, the business may need to operate as a service-area business with the address hidden. Show legitimate business activity without exposing private household information.

### Can a virtual office address be used for Google Maps?

A virtual office or mailbox is generally risky if the business has no real staff, signage, or operations at that location. A shared office can be suitable only when the business genuinely operates there and meets the relevant eligibility conditions. Do not use an address solely to target a city or neighbourhood.

### How long does Google Business Profile verification take?

The time depends on the verification method, the accuracy of the information, and whether Google requests further review. Google does not provide one guaranteed timeline for all Indian profiles. Avoid repeated edits and duplicate submissions while a verification request is being reviewed.

### Can an agency verify a client’s profile?

An agency can help prepare information and manage the profile if the client grants appropriate access. The client should remain the owner or retain ownership of the Business Profile, recovery email, and account security. The agency should not submit documents or make claims that it cannot verify.

## Where to Start

First, confirm that the business is eligible and decide whether it needs a storefront profile or a service-area profile. Then check the real-world business name, address, category, signboard, and existing Google Maps listings.

Collect one or two strong official documents and prepare clear operational evidence. Follow the verification method shown in the GBP dashboard, protect sensitive information, and correct the underlying issue if Google asks for another review.
